subject: WaveHealth: additional projects + API key plan (term adjustment request)
messages:
From: Kate Bruce <kate.bruce@wavehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Lopez <ethan.lopez@wavehealth.com>
Date: 2028-10-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Expanding to 4 new teams — estimate + next steps

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the Q3 ramp support — the pilot is looking solid. Our product org wants to add four additional projects (billing analytics, clinician-chat, triage-bot, and intake-capture) under the same tenant.

Can you send a short note on:
- what the credentialing/API key footprint will look like (per-project keys vs shared namespaces),
- estimated monthly token capacity we should reserve for each project, and
- any impact to our renewal terms/price if we add these now vs at renewal in January?

I've attached a simple sheet with expected monthly volumes per project. Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Kate Bruce
Head of Platform Integrations
WaveHealth

Attachment: WaveHealth_project_list.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42 KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Bruce <kate.bruce@wavehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-20T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 new teams — estimate + next steps

Kate — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Quick notes after a first pass: 

1) Credentialing: we recommend a per-project API key pattern for auditability and least privilege. That will create four new API keys (one per project). If you prefer a namespaced shared key for smaller teams, we can do that too — tradeoff is visibility and ability to revoke per-project.

2) Capacity: based on the volumes you supplied, my estimate is ~60M tokens/month aggregate for the four projects. We can map that to our standard tiering — rough suggestion is add a 70M/mo addendum to cover growth. If you want a strict commitment, we can add this as a reserved capacity tranche under Dedicated; otherwise burstable hosted capacity will work but is less price-predictable.

3) Terms/pricing: adding now (Oct) can be done as a mid-term addendum. There are two paths:
   - Amendment (pro-rated for Nov–Dec) with no contract term change; pricing is standard list for add-on capacity.
   - Move to an early renewal and consolidate (Jan renewal + rate lock) — that would give a 8–12% blended discount on the incremental committed units but requires a 12‑month commit from the amendment date.

I looped in Ben (sales lead) for pricing and Laura (CS) for rollout ops.

If that sounds reasonable, I can push a draft SOW and a proposed pricing addendum (DocuSign link) by EOD Wednesday. Would you prefer per-project keys? Also what is your preferred go-live target?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment references: WaveHealth_project_list.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Bruce <kate.bruce@wavehealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-22T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 new teams — estimate + next steps

Kate — quick follow-up from pricing/strategy side.

We modeled two scenarios (attached in the SOW):
- Option A (Conservative): Add 70M tokens/month as an on-demand addendum (no long-term commitment). Estimated incremental cost: $8.2k/month.
- Option B (Committed): 70M tokens/month reserved for 12 months (starts Nov 1) with an 10% discount on the incremental units. Estimated incremental cost: $6.6k/month (billed monthly).

Additional points:
- If you go with per-project keys we can enable per-key rate limits and usage dashboards per project; that costs no extra but needs an ops readiness window of ~5 business days for key issuance and IAM mapping.
- If you want me to push the committed pricing into a short amendment we can have a signed DocuSign by next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW-wavehealth-expansion-draft.pdf (PDF, 80 KB)

From: Kate Bruce <kate.bruce@wavehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Lopez <ethan.lopez@wavehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-24T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 new teams — estimate + next steps

Thanks Ben — Option B (committed) looks better for our finance forecast. We want per-project keys and per-key dashboards so product can track consumption.

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm a target go-live of Nov 10 (production traffic Nov 13) if we sign the amendment by Nov 2?
2) For the SOW: include a clause that we can add up to 2 additional projects within the first 90 days at the same unit price (we'll need to avoid re-negotiating mid-sprint).

If you can send the amended SOW + DocuSign link today I will route for internal approvals.

Best,
Kate

Date: 2028-10-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 new teams — estimate + next steps

Kate, Ben, Tessa — ops notes for the rollout.

High level timeline if amendment signed by Nov 2: 
- Nov 3: Legal signs DocuSign and billing triggers the capacity addendum.
- Nov 3–7: Provisioning window: create four per-project API keys, set up per-key rate limits, and map to your monitoring workspace.
- Nov 8–9: Smoke test & keys handed to WaveHealth engineers.
- Nov 10: Internal staging cutover.
- Nov 13: Production traffic go-live.

Pre-reqs from WaveHealth:
- One engineering point-of-contact for key rotation and secret storage (we expect an SRE or infra lead).
- Confirm whether each project needs a separate service account or you want a shared service account with distinct keys.
- If you want audit logs exported to your SIEM, share the SIEM endpoint and retention SLA. There may be a small integrator fee for custom log forwarding.

I will include a clause in the SOW for a 90-day addition window for up to 2 projects at the same unit price. Draft SOW attached.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Director | Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW-wavehealth-expansion-draft.pdf
